title: The Sleeping Princess
author: Vasily Zhukovsky
publication_note: a verse fairy tale written in 1831, first printed in 1832 under the title «Tale of the Sleeping Princess»
source_note: Text from ru.wikisource.org, after V. A. Zhukovsky, Collected Works in four volumes, vol. 3 (Moscow–Leningrad, 1960).

names.IV: The Prince and the Old Man

art_alt.1_brook: The sad Queen sits by a brook, and a friendly red crab comes up the bank to tell her good news
art_alt.2_feast: King Matthew's feast: the King and Queen, the baby princess in her cradle, and eleven fairies with their wands
art_alt.3_witch: The grumbling old fairy leans over the cradle, while the young fairy in blue and the King look on
art_alt.4_decree: The King announces his law: no spindles in the kingdom, while the Queen and the little princess listen
art_alt.5_tower: The princess climbs the winding stair of the tower and finds an old woman spinning thread beside a wheel
art_alt.7_asleep: The whole palace sleeps: the King and Queen on the steps, the guards, the cook, the dog and the horse
art_alt.8_thorns: A hundred years later: the palace hidden behind a great leafy hedge under the moon and stars
art_alt.9_old_man: The Prince on his white horse talks with a kind old man at the edge of the wood
art_alt.10_roses: The Prince gallops into the wood where the hedge has turned into blooming roses, with butterflies all around
art_alt.11_courtyard: The Prince in the palace courtyard, where everyone stands or sits fast asleep, and the King sleeps on the steps
art_alt.12_bedroom: The Princess lies asleep in her bed in the tower room, and the Prince stands at the door
art_alt.13_awake: The Prince and the Princess smile in a golden light, while the King and Queen wake up and cheer
art_alt.14_wedding: The wedding feast: the Prince and the Princess with the King, the Queen, three fairies and a wedding cake

figures.caption: King Matthew gives a splendid feast for the baby princess.
figures.caption_ru: Царь Матвей даёт пир в честь царевны.

figures.caption: The King makes a law: no spindles in the whole kingdom.
figures.caption_ru: Царь издаёт указ: во всём царстве не должно быть веретён.

figures.caption: The princess climbs the winding stair and finds an old woman spinning.
figures.caption_ru: Царевна поднимается по винтовой лестнице и видит старушку-пряху.

figures.caption: A great hedge grows round the sleeping palace.
figures.caption_ru: Вокруг спящего дворца вырастает густой бор.

figures.caption: The hedge of thorns turns into roses, and lets the Prince through.
figures.caption_ru: Терновник превращается в розы и пропускает царевича.

figures.caption: In the courtyard, everyone is fast asleep.
The Princess wakes, and the whole palace wakes with her.
figures.caption_ru: Царевна просыпается, а с ней просыпается весь дворец.

figures.caption: A wedding, and a feast for everyone.
figures.caption_ru: Свадьба и пир на весь мир.

glossary: King Matthew
the good King of the tale. In Russian he is Tsar Matvey.
crab
a little animal with claws that lives in streams. In this tale the crab is wise and knows what will happen.
fairy
a magical woman who can give gifts, and make spells. The Russian poem calls them “charodeyki”, enchantresses.
the Uninvited One
the twelfth, old fairy, whom the King forgot to ask to the feast.
spindle
a thin wooden stick, pointed at one end, used long ago to twist wool or flax into thread.
flax
a plant with blue flowers, whose stalks are made into linen thread.
spinner
a person who makes thread, by spinning wool or flax.
courtiers
the people who live at the King's court and wait on him.
standard-bearer
a soldier who carries the flag.
hedge of thorns
a thick, tangled wall of bushes with sharp little thorns.
huntsmen
people who ride out to hunt in the woods and fields.
spurs
little pointed wheels on a rider's boots, used to ask the horse to go faster.
three hundred years
very, very long: longer than ten grandmothers, one after another, could remember.

summary: A good King and Queen have a baby princess, but an old fairy who was not asked to the feast puts a spell on her: when she is sixteen, a spindle will make her sleep for three hundred years. A fairy tale in verse for children, a free retelling of Sleeping Beauty by Vasily Zhukovsky, to be listened to together.
site_description: A King and a Queen long for a child, and a wise crab tells them a princess will be born. But at the feast the twelfth fairy, whom nobody asked, makes a spell: a spindle will send the princess to sleep for three hundred years. The whole palace sleeps behind a wall of thorns, until a young Prince hears the old man's story. Vasily Zhukovsky's gentle retelling of Sleeping Beauty (1831), a fairy tale in verse for children and for listening together, in a full-cast English audiobook with many illustrations.
text_note: Free English verse rendering from the Russian, written for children: a draft that needs a human editor.

ru.description: У доброго царя Матвея и его царицы родилась дочка, но старая чародейка, которую не позвали на пир, заколдовала её: на шестнадцатом году царевна уколется веретеном и уснёт на триста лет. Сказка в стихах Василия Жуковского, вольный пересказ «Спящей красавицы», чтобы слушать вместе с детьми.
